title: Differentiation of Human iPSCs into Microglia-like Cells
author: Jae-Hyeon Park
materials: Maintain iPSCs on Matrigel-coated plates in E8 medium.
Avoid cultures with high spontaneous differentiation.
Warm all media and reagents to room temperature or 37°C as appropriate.

steps.title: Check iPSC confluence
steps.instruction: Verify that iPSC cultures are healthy and approximately 70–80 % confluent before starting differentiation.

steps.title: Prepare Embryoid Body Medium
steps.instruction: Make Embryoid Body Medium (EBM) in E8 medium containing ROCK inhibitor 10 µM, BMP‑4 50 ng/mL, SCF 20 ng/mL, and VEGF‑121 50 ng/mL.

steps.title: Prepare Hematopoietic Medium
steps.instruction: Make Hematopoietic Medium (HM) in X‑VIVO 15 supplemented with GlutaMAX 2 mM, β‑Mercaptoethanol 55 µM, M‑CSF 100 ng/mL, and IL‑3 25 ng/mL.

steps.title: Prepare Microglia Maturation Medium
steps.instruction: Make Microglia Maturation Medium (MMM) in Advanced RPMI supplemented with GlutaMAX 2 mM, IL‑34 100 ng/mL, and GM‑CSF 10 ng/mL.

steps.title: Dissociate iPSCs to single cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate iPSC culture medium, wash cells once with PBS, add TrypLE Express, incubate at 37 °C until cells detach (≈5–10 min), then gently triturate to obtain a single‑cell suspension. Avoid harsh pipetting to preserve viability.

steps.title: Plate cells for embryoid bodies
steps.instruction: Count cells, then seed them into ultra‑low attachment 96‑well plates at 100 µL EBM per well. Return the plate to the incubator.

steps.title: Day 1 media change (remove ROCK inhibitor)
steps.instruction: From each well, remove 80 µL of medium and replace with 100 µL fresh EBM lacking ROCK inhibitor. Pipette slowly at the edge of the well to avoid aspirating embryoid bodies.

steps.title: Day 2–3 daily media changes
steps.instruction: For two consecutive days, perform full media changes by removing the existing medium and adding fresh EBM without ROCK inhibitor (≈20 min per well). Expect embryoid bodies to remain compact and increase slightly in size.

steps.title: Transfer EBs to hematopoietic culture
steps.instruction: Using wide‑bore tips, collect embryoid bodies from the 96‑well plate, transfer them into a conical tube, and allow them to settle by gravity. Carefully remove the supernatant, then transfer approximately 200 EBs into a T75 flask containing 20 mL HM. Return the flask to the incubator.

steps.title: Feed hematopoietic cultures
steps.instruction: Replace the hematopoietic medium with fresh HM every 2 days (≈15 min per feeding). Floating progenitor‑like cells should begin to emerge over time.

steps.title: Monitor microglia progenitor emergence
steps.instruction: Begin observation on Day 10; microglia progenitor cells (MPCs) typically appear between Days 12–18 as large, round, refractive floating cells in the supernatant.

steps.title: Collect microglia progenitors
steps.instruction: Collect the culture supernatant containing floating MPCs, transfer to conical tubes, centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min, aspirate the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in MMM.

steps.title: Seed progenitors for terminal differentiation
steps.instruction: Plate approximately 4 × 10⁶ cells per T75 flask into non‑coated 75 cm² flasks. Add MMM to a final volume of 15–20 mL, then return the flasks to the incubator.

steps.title: Differentiate progenitors into iMGLs
steps.instruction: Culture the cells in MMM for 10 days (240 h total), performing full media changes every other day. Expect progressive microglial morphology with increased adherence, branching, and expression of markers CD11b, CX3CR1, IBA1, P2RY12, and TMEM119.
